facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Lishulong was discovered in 2007 in Jiudu Village, Lufeng County, Yunnan Province, China.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, LFGT-ZLJ0011, was discovered in 2007 in Jiudu Village in Konglongshan Town (formerly named Chuanjie Township), Lufeng County, Yunnan Province, China

facts.statement: The genus name Lishulong means "chestnut tree dragon" and combines the Chinese words for chestnut tree and dragon.
facts.quote: The generic name, Lishulong, combines the Mandarin Chinese words 栗樹/栗树(lìshù)—meaning "chestnut tree"—after the name of the type locality, with 龍/龙 (lóng), meaning "dragon"

facts.statement: The species name wangi honors Wang Zheng-Ju for his contributions to vertebrate paleontology in the Lufeng region.
facts.quote: The specific name, wangi, honors Wang Zheng-Ju, the discoverer of Lufengpithecus, for his contribution to vertebrate paleontology in Lufeng

facts.statement: The holotype specimen consists of a skull, lower jaw, and nine neck vertebrae.
facts.quote: It consists of a cranium, mandible, and nine cervical vertebrae

facts.statement: The first preserved cervical vertebra (axis) has a centrum measuring 16.3 cm in length.
facts.quote: The cervical vertebrae are very large and elongated; the centrum of the first preserved cervical vertebra (the axis) is 16.3 cm long

facts.statement: The tenth preserved cervical vertebra has a centrum measuring 19.9 cm in length.
facts.quote: the centrum of the last preserved cervical vertebra (the tenth consecutive bone in the series) is 19.9 cm long

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Lishulong within the Sauropodiformes as the sister taxon to Yunnanosaurus.
facts.quote: Zhang et al. (2024) included Lishulong in a phylogenetic analysis and found it to be a member of the Sauropodiformes, as the sister taxon to Yunnanosaurus

facts.statement: Lishulong lived approximately between 199 and 183 million years ago, spanning the Sinemurian to Toarcian stages.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 199 a 183 millones de años, desde el Sinemuriense al Toarciense

facts.statement: The time range for Lishulong is estimated from 199.5 to 174.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Sinemurian to Toarcian (199.5 to 174.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fragments of the posterior skeleton were found but were lost during the excavation process.
facts.quote: Parts of the posterior skeleton were also discovered but were lost during excavation

facts.statement: The fossil site of Lishulong is near the discovery location of the theropod dinosaur Panguraptor.
facts.quote: The type locality is close to where the fossils of the coelophysoid theropod Panguraptor were discovered
